title: Stock Labels
story: Staff want a quick label per book: sold out, low (1 to 3 copies) or ok.
goal: Show title and a status column: 'sold out' when copies = 0, 'low' when copies is 1 to 3, otherwise 'ok'.
setup:
CREATE TABLE books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT, year INTEGER, price REAL, copies INTEGER DEFAULT 1);
INSERT INTO books VALUES (1,'Chilaka Learns Loops','Asha',2023,199.0,4),(2,'The Banyan Algorithm','Ravi',2021,349.0,2),(3,'Debugging the Monsoon','Meena',2024,275.0,6),(4,'Seeds of Python','Kiran',2022,150.0,10),(5,'Night Shift SRE','Lakshmi',2020,420.0,0);

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: CASE WHEN condition THEN value ... ELSE value END builds a label per row.
Check copies = 0 first, then copies <= 3, then ELSE.
SELECT title, CASE WHEN copies = 0 THEN 'sold out' WHEN copies <= 3 THEN 'low' ELSE 'ok' END AS status FROM books;
socratic: Which condition should be checked first?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT title, CASE WHEN copies = 0 THEN 'sold out' WHEN copies <= 3 THEN 'low' ELSE 'ok' END AS status FROM books;
alt: SELECT title, CASE WHEN copies = 0 THEN 'sold out' WHEN copies BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN 'low' ELSE 'ok' END AS status FROM books;
